subject: maths
question: P, Q, and R working separately can do a piece of work in 50, 100, and 300 days respectively. If they work on alternate days, P works on the first day, Q works on the second day, R works on the third day and then again P works on the fourth day and so on, then in how many days, the work will be completed?
solution:
**Given**

P can do the work in 50 days

Q can do the work in 100 days

R can do the work in 300 days

**Concept:**

Work done is the inverse of the time taken to complete the work. Total work done in one cycle (3 days) is the sum of work done by P, Q, and R in one day.

**Solution:**

⇒ Work done by P in one day = 1/50

⇒ Work done by Q in one day = 1/100

⇒ Work done by R in one day = 1/300

⇒ Total work done in one cycle (3 days) = (1/50) + (1/100) + (1/300) = 1/30

⇒ Time taken to complete one whole work = 3/(1/30) = 90 days

**Therefore, the work will be completed in 90 days.**
